title: ${MC}{3}$: Memory Contention-Based Covert Channel Communication on Shared DRAM System-on-Chips
problem: Exploiting memory contention in shared DRAM SoCs without last-level cache for high-throughput covert communication. Prior attacks required LLC or privileged/physical access; mobile SoCs lack LLC, creating unexploited vulnerability.
motivation: Shared memory in mobile SoCs enables cost-effective multi-core/accelerator design but creates security threat; high-throughput covert channels compromise sensitive information.
method: Novel MC³ attack targeting shared system memory directly through DRAM contention patterns. Evaluates throughput-robustness tradeoff by modulating contention signals.
key_novelty: High-throughput covert communication via DRAM contention without requiring LLC, privileged access, or irradiation.
contributions: Novel memory-contention-based covert channel on shared DRAM
Achieved 6.4 Kbps transmission rate with <1% error on NVIDIA Orin platforms
Demonstrated feasibility without LLC or elevated system privileges
limitations: Validation limited to NVIDIA Orin variants; generalization to other mobile SoC architectures not discussed.
